summary: Admit the existing mTLS-verified SBP payment webhook through the shared public payment receiver.

impacts.evidence: The shared public receiver resolves organization, workspace and active payment account before invoking the account-scoped verifier.
Only normalized delivery evidence and body digest leave the callback path; raw body and certificate material remain transient.
The existing provider-neutral public webhook route is reused; no OpenAPI path or payload changes.
No event schema or event name changes are introduced.
A previously declared SBP capability is admitted by the generated runtime support projection.
Existing payment webhook evidence and payment status tables are reused.
Verification is an account-scoped mTLS status re-fetch; inbound status and optional signature header are not trusted.
The callback uses the existing validated payment transition path and adds no new privileged mutation.
Existing webhook evidence and canonical payment mutation audit are used for admitted SBP deliveries.
Existing delivery evidence deduplication prevents repeated status changes.
The host-owned SBP mTLS status re-fetch remains bounded by the connector transport and fixed gateway configuration.
Existing public webhook logging, rate limits and payment gateway timeout handling cover SBP.
Removing the single support capability disables SBP webhook admission without a migration or provider mutation.
Registry admission, connector verification and shared route replay/error tests cover repository behavior; live bank delivery remains external qualification.
